text:
olivia: saw a nasty case in prod where multiple routes ended up with identical normalized buckets and traffic bounced between two tiny zones.

chen: is this the old bucketize->winsorize collapse?

olivia: yes. we quantize scores into 16 bins, but small deltas get lost after cost slope and region penalty. result: many routes share same bucket.

diego: simplest fix is a deterministic tie-breaker in evaluator so we don't fall back to list order.

nora: agree. design sketch: compiler emits a 16-bit tie_key per route (stable hash of route_id + region shard) and runtime comparator compares tuple (bucket_id, cost_rank, p95_latency_rank, tie_key). lexicographic and cheap.

chen: allow tenant-level comparator_spec so latency-first tenants can swap cost/lat ordering?

olivia: yes but require explicit opt-in. default: cost then latency. add validator for comparator spec.

diego: anti-flap idea: if chosen route capacity < cap_threshold, start a soft-hold of 30s for that tenant unless new candidate is better by N buckets. prevents oscillation.

nora: telemetry: policy.tie_resolutions.total, policy.tie_resolutions.by_field, policy.flap_held.count. instrument dominance so we can tune ordering.

chen: perf constraints: comparator must be O(1), use uint16s in proto to avoid allocations; target <200ns per comparison.

olivia: rollout: behind ff tie_breaker_v1; unit tests + sim for captured small/large/eu case; canary 1% tenants -> 5% -> full. include enterprise opt-out flag legacy_nondet_routing.

diego: i'll open compiler PR to emit tie_key and proto changes. include bench.

nora: i'll add sim scenarios and dashboard panels for tie_resolutions and flap_rate.

policy-bot: created issue #PLAT-1517: "tie-breaker + anti-flap rollout".

olivia: thanks all. aim to land RFC addendum + PRs by EOW so SRE can review before canary.
